outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: The Challenge of Efficient Foundation Model Adaptation
outline.description: This chapter introduces the context of large-scale foundation models, the prohibitive cost of training from scratch, and the necessity for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT). It reviews existing PEFT paradigms (Model Finetuning, Adapters, Prompt Tuning) and focuses critically on Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT), explaining its principles, advantages in stability/generalization, and its primary limitation: high parameter count due to dense orthogonal matrices.
subtopics: Limitations of Training Foundation Models from Scratch
Overview of PEFT Paradigms: Finetuning, Adapters, and Prompting
The Principles of Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT): Preserving Neuron Angles
The Parameter Efficiency Problem: Why OFT Requires Many Parameters
Review of Block-Diagonal OFT: Trade-offs between Sparsity and Expressivity

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: An Information Transmission Framework for Matrix Factorization
outline.description: This chapter presents the novel theoretical shift proposed in the paper: viewing the construction of an orthogonal matrix as an information transmission problem. It defines a grid-structured graph where matrix factorization corresponds to transmitting information from source nodes to receiver nodes over intermediate layers, providing a unified perspective to design sparse patterns.
subtopics: Preliminaries on OFT Reparameterization and Cayley Transform
Formulating Matrix Factorization as Information Transmission on Grid Graphs
Visualizing Sparsity Patterns via Directed Edges in Information Flow
Desiderata for Efficient Orthogonal Parameterization: Dense Connectivity vs. Minimum Free Edges
The Role of Orthogonality Constraints on Edge Dependencies

outline.description: The core technical chapter detailing the proposal of BOFT. It explains how inspirations from the Cooley-Tukey Fast Fourier Transform lead to 'butterfly factors.' The chapter defines recursive butterfly matrices, details how to parameterize them as orthogonal matrices using block structures, and derives the complexity benefits ($\mathcal{O}(d \log d)$ parameters vs $\mathcal{O}(d^2)$).
subtopics: Inspiration from Cooley-Tukey Algorithm and Butterfly Graph Topology
Defining Butterfly Factors and Recursive Butterfly Matrices

Orthogonalizing Butterfly Components via Cayley Transform and Block Structures

Special Cases: How BOFT Recovers Block-Diagonal OFT as a Subcase
